questions.question: A flywheel of radius 0.5 m rotates at a constant speed of 300 revolutions per minute. Find its angular velocity, the linear speed of a point on the rim and the centripetal acceleration there.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Convert rpm to rad/s:**
$$\omega = \frac{300 \times 2\pi}{60} = \frac{600\pi}{60} = 10\pi$$
$$\omega = \mathbf{31.4\ \text{rad/s}}$$

**Step 2 — Linear (tangential) speed** of a point on the rim:
$$v = \omega r = 31.4 \times 0.5$$
$$\boxed{v = \mathbf{15.7\ \text{m/s}}\approx 15.7\ \text{m/s}}$$

**Step 3 — Centripetal acceleration:**
$$a_c = \frac{v^2}{r} = \omega^2 r$$
$$a_c = \frac{(15.7)^2}{0.5} = \frac{246.49}{0.5} = 492.98\ \text{m/s}^2$$
$$\boxed{a_c \approx \mathbf{493\ \text{m/s}^2}}$$

**Direction:** The acceleration is directed **towards the centre** (along the radius) and hence is a centripetal acceleration; its magnitude stays constant while the velocity direction changes continuously.
questions.knowledgeNote: Angular velocity equals 2 pi n over 60, linear speed equals omega times radius, and centripetal acceleration equals omega squared times radius.
